what_happened: Compiled axiom probes showed the choice-freeness crux is scrubbable: replacing eq_or_ne with Decidable.eq_or_ne in the reflection law makes the whole H_F-membership bridge (reflection -> taskRel_eq_iter -> respects_of_isStepPath -> worldHistoryOfStepPath -> mem_HF_iff_adjacent) measure [propext, Quot.sound] at D = intOrder. Verified by probe, not argued.

Large parts of all three deliverables already exist: FrameOver.extend_periodic / extend_periodic_of_finite_domain (frame level, [Finite W]), IntPresentation.extend_periodic / extend_periodic_of_icc / extend_periodic_extends (certificate level), PlacedBiLasso as the prefix-plus-cycle-each-way certificate, and Agreement.lean already labels one result 'the Deliverable-3 statement'. The task's genuinely new content is the named SFT identification, the choice-free restatement, and repointing stale paper-anchor provenance.

Two provenance records point at the wrong file: Agreement.lean's module docstring says the footnote is in JPL/possible_worlds.tex, and docs/reference/paper-definitions-of-record.md's Untracked sources entry gives JPL/possible_worlds.tex line 1648. The footnote is now cut to JPL/appendix_cut_material.tex and its text has been re-split into separate sentences, so the 'verbatim' quote no longer matches. The same record entry also names FormalSystem.Semantics.TaskFrame.extend_periodic, but the declaration is FormalSystem.Semantics.FrameOver.extend_periodic.

Research recommended relocating the session scratchpad probes into specs/797_.../evidence/; scripts/check-evidence-probes.sh rules explicitly that a probe must NOT live under a task directory (archived task dirs are gitignored, which stranded four probes once already). Plan drops the relocation and pins the same measurements via an in-build #guard_msgs test instead.

Research recommendation 4 implied deliverable (2) lands under Semantics/; no file under FormalSystem/Semantics/ imports FormalSystem.Metalogic, and the choice-free pigeonhole the report tells us to reuse (exists_dup_lt) lives under Metalogic/Decidability/. Plan relocates deliverables (2) and (3) to flat modules under Metalogic/Decidability/ rather than duplicating the pigeonhole.

The research report's three compiled feasibility probes (reflection scrub, computable successor, enumerated pigeonhole) plus its statement-level Nat.card measurement fixed every statement shape in advance, so the plan commits to exact signatures in a Lean Challenge Statements block with no sorry-deferral anywhere and no open feasibility question outside the Mathlib dictionary phase.

Every phase commit that changes a .lean file's line count trips the pre-commit typst-sync-check.sh Check 2 gate (formalsystem-line-count drift in typst/generated/status.typ); remedy is 'bash scripts/typst-sync-check.sh --fix' plus staging typst/generated/status.typ alongside each phase's files.

Phase 3's verification bullet demanding no Classical.choice on mem_HF_iff_no_forbidden is jointly unsatisfiable with the Challenge statement it fixes: Forbidden is a negation, so the biconditional's backward direction is double-negation elimination at a Prop-valued relation. Statement implemented verbatim; criterion closed as a Reasoned Exclusion with the measured profile recorded.

scripts/check-metalogic-cycles.sh exits 1 on a SURPLUS upward edge FormalSystem.MinusLanguage.AxiomDischarge -> FormalSystem.Theorems.LinearityDerived. Not attributable to this task: no commit here touches MinusLanguage/ or Theorems/, and git log dates the edge to commit ba6c0f5dd from a different task. Reported, not fixed.

Four distinct Classical.choice leak families were found by measuring rather than by inspection, each cleared in minutes once located: Mathlib's eq_or_lt_of_le, omega on a goal mentioning Int.emod, every lemma in Mathlib Data/List/GetD.lean, and exact_mod_cast on a bare Nat-to-Int inequality. All four are now pinned by in-build guards so they cannot creep back. Measuring each new declaration immediately after it compiled, rather than at the end of the phase, is what kept each fix local.
